about: Annotated films and bad-to-fixed pairs. Each film is a story that passes `engine check`; its entry says what the story asked for, why the scenes have this shape, what was turned down and what to take from it. Copy the reasoning, not the scenes: `engine gallery --examples` rotates which ones you are shown.

films.asked: A gas cut: how many households, when it starts and ends, which districts, and why.
films.shape: hook, stat, timeline, where, sources, end. One number carries the story (stat), the window is two clock times (timeline), the district is a place (where), the outlets close it (sources).
films.turned_down: trend and share (6400 has no history and is not a part of a whole); versus (nobody is compared); a quote scene (the utility is paraphrased, no sentence is worth quoting).
films.learn: Pick the scene for the shape of the fact: a count is stat, a from-to window is timeline, a place is where.

films.asked: The same outage told as what a household should do.
films.shape: hook, points, steps, sources, end under the brief director: the facts become a short list, then the order of actions.
films.turned_down: stat as the second scene (the director's rule is procedure first); a map (the reader is told what to do, not where it is).
films.learn: A director changes the shape of the same facts; the facts and the news rules do not change.

films.asked: The same outage for a reader who wants the numbers first.
films.shape: hook, stat, timeline, sources, end under the data director: the count opens, the window follows, no list.
films.turned_down: points (it would repeat the narration as bullets); where (the data director draws figures, not places).
films.learn: When the story is a number and a time, two scenes are enough: do not add a third just to fill the length.

films.asked: The same outage for a reader who asks where.
films.shape: hook, where, sign, timeline, end under the map director: the place comes first, a pictogram says the action, the window closes.
films.turned_down: stat (the count is in the narration); sources as a card (the end card carries the outlets).
films.learn: A map scene draws a region of Georgia from the pack's one outline; for crime it never marks a district (geo.PRIVATE).

films.asked: A president proposes a meeting and says why, in his own words.
films.shape: hook, who, quote, where, points, sources, end. The person is named once (who), the sentence is verbatim in a quote scene, the city is a place.
films.turned_down: an opinion scene (never: news stays factual); stat (no number carries the story); paraphrasing the sentence (a quote must be verbatim).
films.learn: A quote scene holds one sentence taken word for word; the writer never improves it.

films.asked: Two checked stories of the morning in one film.
films.shape: hook, then each story's own scenes, a chapter card between them, end. The digest is built by code from stories that already passed, never by a model, and says its real story count.
films.turned_down: a summary scene written by a model (code owns the digest); a third story (only two were checked).
films.learn: A rubric is a named show: its chip, slot and episode number belong to code.

films.asked: How prices and inflation moved, for a reader who wants the picture, not a headline.
films.shape: hook as a question, stat (3.8 percent), pair (food against services), points (what the bank does), end. The explainer program may explain; every number still has to come from its source.
films.turned_down: trend (there is no series in the sources, and a line with two points claims more than the data); share (3.8 is not a part of a whole).
films.learn: An explainer relaxes the news clock, never the claims tier: a number you cannot source is a number you do not draw.

films.asked: What one article of the constitution says, in plain words.
films.shape: hook, quote (the article's own sentence), points (what it protects), pair (right against limit), end. The program law carries its source and link as data.
films.turned_down: a stat (an article number is a name, not a measure); a model's paraphrase of the law inside quotation marks.
films.learn: For a law the quote is the article; the writer explains around it and never rephrases inside the marks.

films.asked: A tiny tale about a robot who learns to draw, for children.
films.shape: hook, steps (the days), points (what Bipi learned), end. The story program has no news rules and a gentler pace; the pack is SiTech's.
films.turned_down: stat (a tale has no figure); where (no real place); a moral spelled out as an opinion scene.
films.learn: Structure carries the feeling: steps show repetition, which is the whole story of learning.

films.asked: A report that attackers used AI assistants against banks, for a technical audience.
films.shape: hook, stat (400 banks and payment apps), points (how it worked), end, in the SiTech pack (paper and coal tones, one orange accent).
films.turned_down: a where scene (the targets span a continent; a map would imply a place); icons for the attack (nothing about harm is pictured, rule N10).
films.learn: A pack changes colour and voice, not the rules: the same scene types, the same checks.

films.asked: The day's one figure, as a short recurring show.
films.shape: hook with the rubric chip, stat, timeline, end in 20 to 25 seconds. The chip, the episode number and the length window belong to the rubric, not the writer.
films.turned_down: points and where (the rubric is one figure and its window; more scenes break the 20 to 25 second promise).
films.learn: A rubric narrows the menu on purpose: its sameness from day to day is the brand, the variety is inside the scene.

films.asked: A tour of the economy scenes: a rank, a contest, a budget split and an impact.
films.shape: hook, ranking, versus, budget, impact, end. Each scene is the one shape its fact has: ordered places, two sides, parts of a total, a before and after.
films.turned_down: bars for everything (they hide that the budget parts sum to a total, which budget draws); stat for the ranking (it loses the order).
films.learn: When one scene type has a sibling that draws the exact shape, use the sibling: ranking over bars, budget over share.

pairs.what: A closing line with an exclamation mark
pairs.why: The news voice states, it does not shout; the check refuses "!", "?", "..." and dashes in the narration.
pairs.fix: End the sentence with a full stop; if the line needs energy, move it into a stronger fact.

pairs.why: The kicker has a Georgian length limit (24) so it fits one line in the safe zone; a longer text is cut or wraps into the headline.
pairs.fix: Say the place alone in the kicker; the action belongs in the hook lines.

pairs.what: A story that opens on a stat
pairs.check_says: the first scene must be a hook
pairs.why: The hook holds the first second: it carries the date chip, the source and the headline. A number alone has no context yet.
pairs.fix: Open with the hook and let the stat be the second scene.

pairs.what: A scene whose `at` is not in the narration
pairs.why: `at` is the exact first words of the part of the narration the scene draws; the timing of the whole film hangs on it.
pairs.fix: Copy the first words of the sentence from the narration, character for character.

pairs.what: A split-flap board on a politics story
pairs.check_says: style 'flap' is not used for the politics family
pairs.why: A flap board is playful; for politics and crime a stat counts up or rolls, it never clatters (the brush's `deny`).
pairs.fix: Leave `style` out (the default count) or choose wheel.

pairs.what: A mark on a phrase the scene does not show
pairs.why: `em` marks words in the scene's own text and the voice lands on them; a phrase that is not there is a mark on nothing.
pairs.fix: Copy the words from the on-screen text; for a stat the value (6400) is the usual choice.
